title: Multiverse
description: Multiverse, the multiverse look, puts the same person in parallel rooms, grades, and costumes at once, so one life is not the inventory. Versions must be separable: a double-exposure mush is not the recipe.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Choice, regret, comic overload: two or three worlds sharing a frame, identity locked so the gag is not strangers. Architecture can repeat with variations.
Each copy has a world, not just a ghost. A single honest scene does not need copies.
It is the wrong tool when you cannot name the worlds, or when failure has no stake. Complexity is not a substitute for knowing what a wrong door costs.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Lock a frame that can hold two or three distinct setups: split architecture, layered rooms, or repeating corridors. Same face, different wardrobe and grade, no mixed features.
Define entry and exit cues. Prompt: Multiverse split of [Subject], many versions, many grades, the same person in parallel rooms.

blocks.text: A choice that forks, a regret that shows the other life, comic overload of selves. Do not use it on a scene that is already one honest room.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Same person, separable worlds. Multiverse split of [Subject], many versions, many grades, the same person in parallel rooms.
Add two or three wardrobes, two or three grades, architecture repeating with variations, identity locked. No mush.

Plan three connected worlds: a real hospital room, a dreamed railway station and a deeper childhood kitchen. Give each one distinct sound, light and a recurring object. A falling cup in the hospital creates a distant rumble in the station and a tremor in the kitchen. Generate and edit the levels separately with a consistent causal map.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: Double-exposure mush, or copies that look like strangers. The tell is blended faces and unnamed worlds.
Fix it: separable versions, locked identity, a stake if a door is wrong.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Multiverse in film?
A parallel-inventory look: the same person in distinct rooms, grades, and costumes at once. Each copy has a world. Mush is failure.
Multiverse vs Split Screen

Split screen is a frame division that can show two actions. Multiverse is the content law: parallel lives, distinct grades, one identity. You can use split screen to hold it, but split screen alone is not the look.
When should I use Multiverse?
Choice, regret, comic overload. Skip a single honest scene, and skip puzzles with no cost of failure.
How do I prompt Multiverse for AI image or video?
Lock identity, then: Multiverse split of [Subject], many versions, many grades, the same person in parallel rooms. Name two or three separable worlds. No blended faces.
